lesson.menu_desc: Asking, chasing and agreeing a deadline, from both sides of the table -- 13 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 7 -- Two Teams
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Joyce Michalczuk | Lesson 7 -- Two Teams

listenings.text: I have been on the provider side for fifteen years. I manage accounting teams that work for other companies, and I will tell you a secret. My people do not work harder for the client who shouts. They work harder for the client who explains. When a manager says, I need this by Friday, my team hears pressure. When she says, I need this by Friday because the auditors arrive on Monday, my team hears a reason, and they will stay late without being asked. So give me the why, give me a real date, and tell me early. A deadline without a reason is just noise.

I have managed external providers for ten years, and I have learned to be friendly and firm at the same time. Friendly is easy. Firm is where most managers fail. They say, if possible, when you have time, no rush. And then the file arrives late, and they are surprised. So I do three things. I say the date clearly, with the hour. I put it in writing the same day. And I say what happens if it is late. Not as a threat, as a fact. If it is late, I am going to miss the close. People respect a clear line. What they do not respect is a line that moves.
